[USER] User needs help setting up automatic backups for working files.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Recommended backup software options:  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 1. Backblaze: Cloud-based backup service that automatically backs up files. (Windows, Mac, Linux)  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 2. Acronis True Image: Comprehensive backup solution with local and cloud options, disk imaging, and ransomware protection. (Windows, Mac)  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 3. Carbonite: Cloud-based backup service with automatic backup and external hard drive options. (Windows, Mac)  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 4. CrashPlan: Cloud-based backup service with automatic backup and external hard drive options. (Windows, Mac, Linux)  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 5. Time Machine: Built-in backup solution for Macs that backs up files to an external hard drive.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 6. Windows Backup: Built-in backup solution for Windows for system image and file backups.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 7. Duplicati: Free, open-source backup software with local and cloud options, encryption, and versioning. (Windows, Mac, Linux)  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 8. Areca Backup: Free, open-source backup software with local and cloud options, encryption, and versioning. (Windows, Mac, Linux)  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 9. IDrive: Cloud-based backup service with automatic backup and external hard drive options. (Windows, Mac)  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] 10. Google Drive (Google One): Cloud storage service with automatic backup options. (Web, Android, iOS)  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Suggested factors to consider when choosing backup software: ease of use, automatic backup, storage capacity, security, compatibility, and features.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Explained the 3-2-1 backup rule: three copies of data, two different storage types, and one offsite copy.  
[USER] User is leaning towards Backblaze and asks about file versioning.  
[ASSISTANT_SAID] Explained Backblaze's file versioning: keeps version history for up to 30 days, stores multiple versions, and offers restore options via web interface or desktop application.
